answers.text: Nothing changed. I ran out of days.
answers.reply: He nods at the window. The days are still out there. He doesn't say so.

answers.text: Someone needed the day more than I did.
answers.reply: He looks at your hands for a while, as if checking what they gave away.

answers.text: I stopped wanting it and didn't notice.
answers.reply: He writes something small and does not show you.
He smiles at that, the way you smile at a child who has lied well.

questions.text: Who did you think of first, this morning?

answers.reply: He seems to find that honest, and honesty seems to tire him.

answers.text: Someone out there in the cold.
answers.reply: He turns his head toward the cold, as though he can hear them from here.

answers.text: No one. I just got up.
answers.reply: He takes that the way he takes everything: without hurry.

questions.text: Was it worth what it cost you?

answers.reply: He laughs once, quietly. Tomorrow is a joke only the two of you share.

answers.text: No. But I'd do it again.
answers.reply: He sets his cup down very gently, and leaves it there.

answers.text: I don't know what it cost.
answers.reply: He holds up nothing, and looks at it, and puts it away.

answers.text: Nothing costs anything here. It all comes back.
answers.reply: He doesn't argue. He touches the wall, which is older than it was.

questions.text: Could you still say their name?

answers.reply: He waits, in case you'll say it now. You don't.
He nods. Mornings are where names live, he seems to think.

answers.text: Does it matter, if the day starts over?
answers.reply: He studies you a long moment, the way you'd study a stopped clock.

questions.text: Tomorrow you'll have the same hours. Same order?

answers.reply: He folds his hands. Something in how he does it is approving, and something isn't.
He shifts his chair a little, to see which way you'll go.
He glances at the dark past the window, measuring how far further is.
He lets the quiet sit there between you, unplanned.
He seems glad of it, and sorry, both at once.
He nods slowly. Hoping is something he's watched before.
He bows his head, very slightly, as if that were a kindness.

questions.text: The little one waited up. Where were you?

answers.text: Out. Doing things that mattered more.
answers.reply: He looks at the small coat on its hook, and says nothing about it.

answers.text: I thought there'd be another evening.
answers.reply: He counts the evenings on his fingers and stops before the end.

answers.text: I didn't know they were waiting.
answers.reply: He looks toward the little bed as though it had told him otherwise.

questions.text: What did you hope they'd become?

answers.reply: He tilts his head. Better is a long road, he seems to say.
He looks at the door, and then at you, and then at the door.
He waits, as if you might think that far now. The room stays quiet.

answers.text: Whatever they wanted. Not what I wanted.
answers.reply: He nods, and for a moment he looks almost fond of you.

breaks.text: Aldo had the shop, and the debt, and a daughter on the coast. You had a word with his creditor. You gained a morning. He lost the forty years behind that counter, and the coast he was going to see. That one is finished now. It does not start again tomorrow.

self: You had the same day, every day, and you spent it on yourself.
That is not nothing — you were owed a life too.
But the town went on around you, and it went on without you in it.
others: You had the same day, every day, and you gave it away.
It cost you. You can see what it cost you.
They kept what you gave them; that part did not start over.
